title: Djokovic recovers from a tough start to extend Beijing winning run
summary:
Novak Djokovic kept his unbeaten record in Beijing after a demanding comeback against China's Bu Yunchaokete. The six-time champion recovered from losing the opening set to win 4-6, 7-6 (7-2), 6-2 and reach the China Open's third round.

The result took Djokovic's record in Beijing to 31 matches without a defeat. This victory required two hours and 52 minutes of effort, and Bu made the Serbian player work for it.

During the second set, Djokovic lost an advantage he had gained by winning one of Bu's service games. He needed a medical timeout and received a time violation while trying to regain his breath between points. A time violation means a player has taken longer than the rules allow before play continues.

The 39-year-old consulted the trainer, then took control of the tie-break, winning it 7-2. A tie-break is a special scoring game used to settle a close set. Djokovic found his rhythm in the deciding set, won four games in succession and ended the match with a backhand winner.

In the women's event, Aryna Sabalenka began her campaign by beating Mexico's Renata Zarazua 6-1, 6-3. She hit 11 aces and faced no break points, meaning Zarazua never reached a point that could win a game on Sabalenka's serve.

It was Sabalenka's first match since losing her number one ranking and US Open title to Elena Rybakina in September. Her latest tournament title came in Miami in March.

Sabalenka explained that demanding more from herself can drive her forward, but can also drain her energy. She said she was trying to be less self-critical. She was due to face Czech player Nikola Bartunkova next, while Djokovic's next opponent would be Alexander Zverev or Shang Juncheng.
why_it_matters: The match extended Djokovic's unbeaten Beijing record and sent him into the third round. Sabalenka's victory also provided a chance for her to explain the pressures she puts on herself.
